extracted.intended_audience: observational astronomers and spectroscopists; readers of scientific reports (Nature)
extracted.subtask_description: Conducting and reporting visual spectroscopic observations of stellar radial velocities by comparing stellar spectral lines with terrestrial reference lines, including instrumentation, measurement methods, error accounting, and interpretation of motions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instrument specification and quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of an appropriate spectroscope (e.g., spectroscope C containing four compound prisms) and sufficient magnifying power (the author used a magnifying power of 16 diameters).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The quality and configuration of the spectroscope materially affect accuracy; differences in instruments can explain discrepancies with earlier results. Ensure instruments are suitably configured (prisms, magnification) for the small refrangibility changes expected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observational conditions and steadiness
rubrics_metrics.description: Atmospheric movements and unsteady air degrade line visibility; narrow slits make stellar light faint and lines cannot be steadily seen except on very fine nights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform observations on nights of unusual steadiness; favour evenings with fine seeing. Note and report atmospheric steadiness; avoid making precise estimates when air is unfavourable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Slit width and signal considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: A narrow slit increases spectral resolution but reduces stellar light, making lines faint; when slit is narrow the clock’s motion may not be uniform enough to keep the spectrum steadily in view.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance slit width between resolution and brightness; ensure clock drive uniformity when using narrow slits; document slit choice and its effect on line visibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of comparison/reference lines
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare stellar lines with reliable terrestrial lines (hydrogen, sodium, magnesium) and use established solar/terrestrial wavelength tables (Angstrom).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select comparison lines present and strong in both terrestrial tubes and stellar spectra; use known multiplet structures and relative intensities (e.g., sodium double, magnesium triple) to confirm identification before measuring shifts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Line selection suitability
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer spectral lines that are strong, narrow, and well-defined for comparison (e.g., hydrogen lines Hα, Hβ, sodium double, magnesium triplet).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid lines that are faint, broad, or embedded in groups of fine lines; choose the 'most suitable lines' for ascertaining stellar motion and document reasons for selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accounting for blended or composite spectra
rubrics_metrics.description: Spectra of double or multiple stars may blend into one spectrum; the light of both components may combine, complicating comparisons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize and report blending in double-star observations; where spectra blend, note limitations on velocity estimates and, if possible, attempt to disentangle components or avoid blended targets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurement method and estimation technique
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimations of small shifts were made by comparing the shift with a wire of known thickness, or with the interval between a pair of close lines; use of a micrometer was judged to give only the appearance of greater accuracy under the circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose estimation techniques suited to signal/noise and stability: visual comparison to known spacings can be preferable to micrometer readings when micrometer precision is misleading. Describe the method used and justify it given observational limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantification scale for shifts
rubrics_metrics.description: Shifts measured as fractions of known line intervals (e.g., 'one-fifth of the distance of D2 from D1', 'one-sixth of the interval from Mg1 to Mg2'), then converted to velocity using wavelengths and speed of light.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report shifts in fraction-of-interval units and show conversion to velocity (state wavelengths used and speed of light value). Be explicit about the reference interval used for each estimate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constants and wavelength sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Wavelengths employed are those given by Angstrom (Recherches sur le spectre solaire, Upsal, 1868); the velocity of light used was taken as 185,000 miles per second.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State explicitly the wavelength source and numerical constant(s) used in velocity computations so others can reproduce or update calculations with modern values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Error estimation and provisional reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: The probable error of estimations is large because the amount of change of refrangibility is very small; shifts corresponding to about five miles per second could not be certainly observed. The author regards the estimations as provisional and expects to obtain more accurate determinations with improved apparatus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide honest estimates of uncertainty, declare results provisional when warranted, and describe planned improvements or limitations that affect confidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repeat observations and instrument combinations
rubrics_metrics.description: Comparisons were made on several nights and with different spectroscopes and eye-pieces (e.g., spectroscope C with eye-pieces 2 and 3; spectroscope B with eye-piece 3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeat measurements across multiple nights and instrument setups to confirm consistency; report which instrument/eyepiece combinations produced which results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accounting for Earth's orbital motion
rubrics_metrics.description: The earth’s orbital motion at the time of observation was calculated and either added or subtracted from the apparent motion to estimate the star's true motion in the line of sight (tables show 'Earth's motion' and 'Apparent motion').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute and report the Earth's velocity component towards/from each star at observation time; explicitly separate apparent motion and the component due to Earth's orbital motion when reporting stellar radial velocities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of solar motion and group/peculiar motions
rubrics_metrics.description: Observed velocities represent the whole of the motion in the line of sight between the stars and the sun; some part of observed velocities must be due to the solar motion and there may also be a common drift of groups of stars and peculiar motions of individual stars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret radial velocities in the broader kinematic context: consider solar motion, possible group drift, and individual peculiar velocities. State whether and how corrections for solar motion or group membership were attempted (the author did not attempt the solar-motion correction).

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparison with previous observations
rubrics_metrics.description: New observations should be compared with former papers; differences may be due to less perfect instruments earlier or to orbital motions if stars are in elliptical orbits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss agreements and discrepancies with prior work, and attribute differences to instrumentation, observational conditions, or astrophysical causes (e.g., orbital motion) where plausible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Line profile diagnostics (breadth and intensity)
rubrics_metrics.description: The difference in breadth of hydrogen lines in different stars gives information about the density of the gas producing absorption; relative intensities indicate element presence (e.g., sodium lines more intense but within group of fine lines).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use line width and intensity comparisons (to solar spectrum and laboratory lines) to infer physical conditions; report such diagnostics and reserve detailed discussion for further analysis when adequate data are available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification via multiplet structure and relative strengths
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification of elements by matching double/triple character, relative distances, and comparative brightness of groups of lines (e.g., sodium double character agreeing exactly; three lines corresponding precisely to magnesium triple).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm elemental identifications by checking multiplet patterns and relative strengths as seen in terrestrial and solar spectra before using those lines for velocity determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding overinterpretation from artifacts or blending
rubrics_metrics.description: Some nebular or nebulous character assigned to lines may be due to neighbouring very fine lines; minute displacements near detection limits should be treated cautiously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider instrumental, blending, and atmospheric causes for apparent features before concluding physical origins; when displacement is near the detection threshold, qualify conclusions and seek further data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation of results in summary tables
rubrics_metrics.description: Summarize comparisons and motions in tables (e.g., 'TABLE I.—Stars moving from Sun' and 'TABLE II.—Stars approaching the Sun') listing star, compared line, apparent motion, Earth's motion, and deduced motion relative to the sun.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear tabular summaries separating comparison line(s), apparent measured shift, Earth's motion at observation time, and inferred stellar motion; include notes on observational quality for each entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of targets and reporting selection effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Select stars whose spectra have suitable lines for comparison; record when observations for certain stars were unsatisfactory due to poor air or single-night data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document selection rationale and any selection biases (e.g., only nights with fine air give reliable estimates); refrain from definitive claims for targets with insufficient or poor-quality data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Planning for instrumentation and methodological improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: The author notes apparatus now being constructed to get more accurate determinations, implying the need to improve instruments to reduce probable errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State limitations of current apparatus and describe intended improvements (e.g., better spectroscope, more stable clock drive) when reporting provisional results; outline how improvements will reduce uncertainties.
